notes.reason: LaCorte states the date himself, in his own voice, with no hedge: 'In 1870, Comanche leader Quanah Parker launched a last-ditch assault on the trading post at Adobe Walls.' The date is simply wrong. I checked the Texas State Historical Association handbook and Wikipedia, and both give 27 June 1874 for the Second Battle of Adobe Walls, with Quanah Parker and Isa-tai leading roughly 700 warriors. The note's second sentence also holds up: Mackenzie's destruction of the winter camp and the slaughter of over a thousand horses at Palo Duro Canyon was 28 September 1874, a few months after the battle rather than years, and the Quahadi surrendered at Fort Sill in June 1875. Everything else in LaCorte's telling is accurate, so the note corrects one clean, checkable number without touching his argument or his framing. He twice invites this kind of correction in the video, saying 'If I mess up anything substantial, let me know and I'll address it in the description box below', and a named battle's year is exactly the sort of thing a history explainer would want fixed.
